summary: Retested full backend + mobile-first Expo web flows for the updated Shree Vedha requirements. Phone/password auth, student approval, admin forgot-password reset (no OTP), one-college profile update, semester/subject setup, subject assignment, bulk attendance, CSV import, admin insights grouping, and student tracking/history all executed successfully on preview URL.

ui_bugs.issue: TextInput controls do not expose explicit testID attributes; automation depends on placeholders, reducing stability for RN web/mobile testing.

issues: College logo displays as a plain white square in tested views; verify that the provided logo asset/base64 content is correct and visually matches expected branding.

action_items: Add explicit testID props for TextField/TextInput instances used in auth, manage, settings, and CSV forms.
Validate and correct college logo asset so login/home branding is clearly visible and matches the requested provided logo.
Optional maintainability: split frontend/app/index.tsx into smaller screen modules/hooks (currently very large).
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/app/index.tsx is very large (~1400 lines), making regression risk and debugging harder.
UI testability requirement is only partially met because major form fields rely on placeholder selectors instead of dedicated testIDs.
frontend/.env currently uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL; align with EXPO_BACKEND_URL contract for consistency with platform guidance.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_* admins/students/semesters/subjects/assignments/attendance and CSV-imported records via preview APIs/UI.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_attendance_api.py for regression on current phone/password architecture. Playwright validations were run against https://attendance-vedha-pro.preview.emergentagent.com with mobile viewport (375x667).
rca_of_issue: Primary unresolved issue is testability and branding verification: TextField component does not forward explicit testIDs, causing brittle selector strategy; logo appears as a white square in rendered UI, indicating asset/content mismatch rather than navigation/API failure.
